item.title: Staking APY Verification: Does the Advertised Rate Match What You Actually Earn
item.description: Staking product homepages advertise a headline APY, but protocol take-rate, validator commission, compounding assumptions, and token price movement can leave the actual net yield well below the number on the landing page. This piece breaks down a gross-vs-net yield method, a compounding-assumption check, a hidden-risk checklist, and a cross-protocol comparison framework. Not investment advice.

item.title: Open Interest Verification: Is the Surge Real Demand or Stacked Leverage
item.description: A spike in open interest (OI) is often read as rising market heat, but the same number can come from broad new participation or a handful of accounts repeatedly stacking leverage. This piece breaks down how to verify what's really behind OI growth: position concentration, cross-checking against funding rate direction, liquidation price heatmaps, and cross-exchange comparison — so stacked leverage doesn't get mistaken for real demand.

item.title: DAO Grant Verification: "Milestone-Based" on Paper, One Lump Sum On-Chain
item.description: DAO grant proposals almost always promise funds released in stages tied to milestones — it reads like a careful safeguard. But whether those milestones have verifiable objective standards, whether the on-chain transfers actually match the proposed schedule, and where the money goes after landing are three things worth checking independently rather than taking the proposal text at face value.

item.title: Order Book Depth Verification: Why Displayed Liquidity Vanishes Before You Can Hit It
item.description: The depth shown on an order book and the amount you can actually fill at that price are often two different things. This piece breaks down how iceberg orders hide true size, why quotes cancel the instant you click buy, how aggregated depth masks a thin single source, and how researchers can verify displayed depth with repeated snapshots and small probe orders.

item.title: Destination-Chain Sandwich Attacks on Cross-Chain Swaps
item.description: Cross-chain slippage caps are fixed, but the destination price only settles after source confirmation - a delay bots exploit to hit your cap. Verify the gap.
